newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to get $600,000 for nuclear protection.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to get $600,000 for nuclear protection.

text.p: Croatia signed an agreement to receive $600,000 worth of technical aid with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), state agency HINA reported on Monday.

The accord, co-signed by Croatian minister of economy Davor Stern and IAEA deputy general director for nuclear security Zygmund Damaratzki, obliges the Zagreb government to apply certain protection measures against nuclear radiation.
Croatia uses only one nuclear powerplant, located in neighbouring Slovenia, which the two countries co-own.
The agreement also lists measures for protecting nuclear materials against theft and misuse, HINA said.
The accord also envisages additional funds for modernising Croatia's medical radio-therapy. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-457075
